company: Hoshine Silicon Industry Co., Ltd. and subsidiaries
outcome: WRO in force until subsumed by UFLPA on 2022-06-21
description: CBP Withhold Release Order instructing ports to detain silica-based products made by Hoshine and subsidiaries (metallurgical silicon, an upstream polysilicon input). Context: this predates the June 2022 window.

company: Hoshine Silicon Industry (Shanshan) Co., Ltd. and subsidiaries
outcome: On UFLPA Entity List (sub-lists i and v)
description: Named on the initial UFLPA Entity List.

company: Xinjiang Daqo New Energy Co., Ltd.
outcome: On Entity List; added to second sub-list (v) on 2024-11-25
description: High-purity polysilicon producer in Shihezi. Named on the initial June 2022 list (sub-list i). The Nov 2024 action put it on a second sub-list; it was not a new listing.

company: Xinjiang GCL New Energy Material Technology Co., Ltd. (now Xinjiang Goens Energy Technology Co., Ltd.)
outcome: On Entity List; renamed by technical update effective 2026-08-03
description: Polysilicon and monocrystalline silicon producer in Changji. Named on the initial list. The Aug 2026 notice updated the name to Goens. The DHS page now shows 2026-08-03 as its effective date, but that is a rename, not a new listing.

company: Xinjiang East Hope Nonferrous Metals Co., Ltd.
outcome: On Entity List; alias 'Xinjiang Nonferrous' removed 2024-11 (technical correction)
description: Named on the initial list. The DHS page shows a 2024-11-25 effective date because of the correction. Its solar relevance (silicon/aluminium inputs) is context only; the sources here do not describe its products.

company: Not disclosed by CBP (aggregate)
outcome: None released as of 2022-10-25
description: CBP told Reuters (records request) that it had detained 1,053 shipments of solar energy equipment between 2022-06-21 and 2022-10-25. CBP did not name manufacturers.

company: LONGi Green Energy Technology Co., Ltd.
outcome: Not disclosed
description: Industry sources told Reuters that the 1,053 detained solar shipments (up to ~1 GW) were primarily made by LONGi, Trina and JinkoSolar. LONGi did not comment.

company: Trina Solar Co., Ltd.
outcome: Shipments reported clearing by early 2023 (C-011)
description: Named by industry sources as one of the main makers of detained solar shipments in 2022. Trina did not comment at the time.

company: JinkoSolar Holding Co., Ltd.
outcome: Company said it was working with CBP on documentation and was confident shipments would be admitted
description: Named by industry sources. JinkoSolar's own statement to Reuters acknowledged that shipments were under CBP review.

company: JinkoSolar Holding Co., Ltd.
outcome: Some shipments released from detention
description: A source close to the company told Reuters that Jinko shipments had been released.

company: Trina Solar Co., Ltd.
outcome: Trina said >900 MW cleared US customs in the prior four months, with <1% detained for examination
description: Company statement to Reuters, attributed to traceability documentation provided to CBP.

company: LONGi Green Energy Technology Co., Ltd.
outcome: Modules reportedly excluded; LONGi expected to appeal
description: Roth Capital industry note (via pv magazine): CBP excluded LONGi modules made with Tongwei polysilicon. CBP has not confirmed this.

company: Astronergy (Chint New Energy)
outcome: Under review at time of report
description: pv magazine checks: modules made with Astronergy polysilicon detained and under UFLPA review.

company: Donghai JA Solar Technology Co., Ltd.
outcome: On UFLPA Entity List (sub-list v)
description: JA Solar subsidiary (silicon rods, wafers, ingots, cells, modules). Added to the Entity List; FLETF cites sourcing of polysilicon from a XUAR producer. No public JA Solar detention record was found for 2022-23.

company: Hongyuan Green Energy Co., Ltd. (HY Solar)
outcome: On UFLPA Entity List (sub-list v)
description: Added to the Entity List; FLETF cites XUAR polysilicon sourcing.

company: Hongyuan New Materials (Baotou) Co., Ltd.
outcome: On UFLPA Entity List (sub-list v)
description: PV monocrystalline silicon maker; subsidiary of Hongyuan Green Energy. Added to the Entity List.

company: Shuangliang Silicon Materials (Baotou) Co., Ltd.
outcome: On UFLPA Entity List (sub-list v)
description: Added to the Entity List; FLETF cites polysilicon sourced from XUAR producers.

company: Jiangsu Meike Solar Technology Co., Ltd.
outcome: On UFLPA Entity List (sub-list v)
description: Added to the Entity List (Jan 2025 batch, solar/silicon group).

company: Baotou Meike Silicon Energy Co., Ltd.
outcome: On UFLPA Entity List (sub-list v)
description: Added to the Entity List (Jan 2025 batch, solar/silicon group).

company: Maxeon Solar Technologies
outcome: CBP denied protests; Maxeon filed a complaint at the US Court of International Trade in July 2025; modules still held as of Dec 2025
description: CBP denied Maxeon's protests against detentions of more than 160 shipments of solar panels from its Mexico plants (detentions running for almost two years by Dec 2025).

company: Hanwha Qcells
outcome: Imports eventually cleared; ~1,000 Georgia staff furloughed; normal production resumed March 2026
description: Korean-made solar cells for Qcells' Georgia module plants detained under UFLPA. Qcells said its supply chain is sourced outside China. The June 2025 dashboard showed 7 South Korea electronics shipments ($3.37m), the first such from Korea.

company: VSUN (Abalance Group; brand acquired by Toyo in Sept 2025)
outcome: CBP decision confirmed 2026-01-11: 'sufficient evidence to allow for an exception could not be confirmed'; VSUN pursuing through counsel
description: Abalance disclosed the detention of VSUN modules and an expected JPY3-5bn (US$18-31m) earnings impact; this is not a shipment value. Cells likely from Ethiopia, matching an Ethiopia 8541 detention spike in Jan-Feb 2026.

company: TBEA Co., Ltd.
outcome: On UFLPA Entity List (sub-list v)
description: Added in the 187-entity expansion. FLETF basis: aluminium and aluminium alloy products sourced from XUAR. DHS describes TBEA as also producing high-purity polysilicon. Its polysilicon subsidiary Xinte Energy is not separately named.

company: Xinjiang Tianchi Energy Co., Ltd. (TBEA subsidiary)
outcome: On UFLPA Entity List (sub-list v)
description: Coal mining and power generation subsidiary of TBEA; FLETF basis is coal sourced from XUAR. Upstream energy context for polysilicon.
